answer.reason: The verses tell of Hazael's rise to the throne and his oppression of Israel and Judah, beyond what the summary states.

clauses.english: was told by Elisha that he would be king, and the next day reigned after Benhadad died
clauses.quote: he took a thick cloth, and dipped it in water, and spread it on his face, so that he died: and Hazael reigned in his stead.

clauses.english: oppressed Israel, smiting their coasts, in the days of Jehu and Jehoahaz
clauses.quote: Hazael king of Syria oppressed Israel all the days of Jehoahaz.

clauses.english: took Gath and was paid off with the temple treasures so that he left Jerusalem
clauses.quote: Hazael king of Syria went up, and fought against Gath, and took it

doubts: The summary already says he was servant of Benhadad and reigned, so the first clause rests on the prophecy and his accession; the smothering of Benhadad is left unattributed since the verse does not name the doer clearly.
1KI 19:15 (command to anoint Hazael) and the verses about the war at Ramoth-gilead were left out as they only name him or give a command, not a deed of his.
AMO 1:4 is a prophecy of judgment on his house, not an event told, so it was not used.
